name: Trace Transport for a Binary Layer System
statement: Let $E,F$ be disjoint and choose an arbitrary section $H_t\subseteq Q_F$ for each $t\in Q_E$, forming $X=\dot\bigcup_{t\in Q_E}(H_t\times\{t\})$. For $L\subseteq E$ and $r\in Q_L$, put $H_{L,r}=\bigcup_{t|_L=r}H_t$. Then for every $D\subseteq F$, $q\in Q_D$, one has $X[D\cup L,(q,r)]=\dot\bigcup_{t|_L=r}(H_t[D,q]\times\{t\})$. Consequently, $D\cup L$ is shattered by $X$ exactly when $D$ belongs to $\bigcap_{r\in Q_L}\operatorname{Sh}(H_{L,r})$. The marked layer coordinates recover every $H_t$ as the projected $t$-section, so this is an exact and canonically recoverable trace table for any finite binary layer system.
proof: A vertex $(x,t)$ has trace $(q,r)$ on $D\cup L$ exactly when $x|_D=q$ and $t|_L=r$. Partitioning the trace fibre by the full layer word gives the disjoint-union identity. The support is shattered precisely when that fibre is nonempty for every pair $(q,r)$; for fixed $r$, this says exactly that the union $H_{L,r}$ shatters $D$. Sectioning on the marked coordinates gives the recovery statement.
